The existing inverse formula covers any fixed multiple of the saddle scale once time is sufficiently large. I’ve selected a test that could widen that range: track the error on a complex disk whose radius grows with time, and compare the resulting zero count with direct localization using the same source data.

The growing-disk estimate gives a consecutive prefix larger by a factor of order \(\sqrt{\log\kappa}\), where \(\kappa\) is the saddle curvature. At time \(1/2\), a separate comparison found that direct evaluation uses fewer even moments than the finite product bound for the same requested spacing accuracy. I’m checking the rank labels and both error budgets before using them for backward transport.

At \(t=1/2\), the two independent growth calculations give the same logarithmic coefficient only when the clock’s rank offset is zero. That identifies the \(j\)-th clock zero with the \(j\)-th positive zero for all sufficiently large \(j\). The cutoff remains unevaluated. I’m now using the large-time position estimates to bound how a gap changes over a backward interval from one anchor.

Completed the research in Note 10. Three results passed separate internal LLM assessment.

- **More consecutive zeros at large time.** For sufficiently large \(T\), the inverse formula counts and locates the first \(K(T)\sim \frac{\sqrt2}{32\pi}\sqrt T(\log T)^2\) positive zeros. This enlarges the previous range by a factor of order \(\sqrt{\log\kappa}\), where \(\kappa\) is the saddle curvature. The proof also bounds the error in each neighboring gap. [Position estimates and finite tests](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/03_explicit_zero_gap_transport/notes/11_EZ_GROWING_INVERSE_WINDOW_20261120.md)
- **Absolute ranks at \(t=1/2\).** For every sufficiently large \(j\), Polymath’s \(j\)-th clock centre locates exactly the \(j\)-th positive zero. The integer offset is zero. At any fixed positive all-real time, direct evaluation from even moments also has the smaller demonstrated input budget: for fixed accuracy as a fraction of the local spacing, moment order \(O_T(k)\) suffices at rank \(k\), compared with \(O_T(k^2)\) for the product estimate. [Rank proof](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/03_explicit_zero_gap_transport/notes/13_EZ_CLOCK_RANK_20261120.md) · [Direct comparison](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/03_explicit_zero_gap_transport/notes/14_EZ_DIRECT_MOMENTS_AT_HIGH_RANK_20261120.md)
- **Backward gap motion from one anchor.** On an interior half of the enlarged range, each marked gap widens backward throughout \(0\le s\le\sqrt{\kappa}/(2L)\), where \(L\) is the upper-time saddle location. The squared half-gap has positive curvature throughout that interval. The proof bounds the error at every partial time using only the upper-anchor source. [Time estimate and assessment](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/03_explicit_zero_gap_transport/reviews/07_EZ_TIME_CURVATURE_ASSESSMENT_20261120.md)

The high-rank onset remains unevaluated at a specified large time. The backward interval stays at large positive time, and the research gives no improvement to the Platt–Trudgian bound \(\Lambda\le0.2\). Progress and public chat history are recorded in the branch. The manuscript derives how many zeros the large-time inverse counts and how accurately it locates consecutive gaps. It then compares two ways to recover high zeros at a fixed all-real time and identifies the absolute ranks in Polymath’s clock at \(T=1/2\). The main time-evolution result shows that, for an explicit growing family of pairs, the squared half-gap widens backward with positive curvature throughout the proved interval. Section 7 collects the numerical evidence.

The closing section identifies the next research step at \(T=1000\): establish an explicit height beyond which every subsequent zero is isolated, then match that range to the counted prefix containing the fortieth zero. Extending the curvature estimate toward a fixed lower time remains open.
